description.summary: which window is where, and a picture of one, for one trusted client

protocol.description:
A compositor tells no ordinary client where windows are or what they show. This protocol lets one trusted client ask, one window at a time and only while the person is pointing: which window is under the pointer, which window is active, and a picture of the window it was just told about. It exists so a person can point at a window (drag a mark onto it, or press a key while it is active) and ask about that window.
The compositor offers this global only to the client it launched itself as the locator, and starts that client only when its own configuration and the client's program are the system's (root's) alone. It checks the person's gesture itself. It sends nothing unasked: every event answers a request, or (armed) the person's locate key, so the client never learns about a window the person did not point at. Nothing is answered while the session is locked.
The gesture checks hold the launched client to the person's action. They are not a boundary against other programs running as the person, which can synthesize input through the compositor's virtual keyboard and pointer.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental and backward incompatible changes may be made.

interface.name: zyantrik_window_locator_v1

description.summary: the window locator, for the client labwc launched

interface.description:
at and focused each take a serial chosen by the client and are answered by exactly one window or none event carrying that serial, in the order they were made. capture is answered by exactly one picture or capture_failed event naming the same window.
A picture may be taken only of the window named by the most recent answer to at or focused, only while that answer is at most two seconds old, and only once per answer: a none answer, a later window answer or a capture request each use it up, except a capture refused as not_located or throttled. Since at and focused are answered only during the person's gesture, so is capture.
at is answered with a window only while a pointer button is held and x, y are within 8 pixels of the cursor: the person dragging. focused is answered with a window only within two seconds after an armed event, and once per armed. Otherwise the answer is none with reason no_gesture.
A window whose app id is on the compositor's private list is named without its title, with the private flag, and is never pictured.
Window ids are stable while the window exists. An id is given to a window the first time an answer names it, and is not given to another window until 2^32 more have been named.

entry.name: private
entry.summary: on the private list: no title is given and no picture is taken

entry.name: nothing
entry.summary: no window there, something that is not a window (a panel, a dock, a menu) is on top there, or no active window

entry.name: throttled
entry.summary: over 120 at and focused requests in the current one-second window

entry.name: no_gesture
entry.summary: the person is not pointing: no button held at the cursor (at), or no armed in the last two seconds or already answered (focused)

entry.name: not_located
entry.summary: not the window of the most recent answer, that answer is over two seconds old, or it was already used

entry.name: gone
entry.summary: the window closed, was unmapped or minimized, or is no longer on the workspace the person is on

entry.name: throttled
entry.summary: over 2 pictures in the current one-second window

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: the compositor could not draw the picture

entry.name: private
entry.summary: the window is on the private list

request.name: at

description.summary: which window is at this point

request.description: The topmost window drawn at x, y in layout coordinates, counting its decorations and popups, on the workspace the person is on. Answered only during the person's drag (see the interface description). The client's own surfaces are looked through, so a full-screen overlay it draws during the drag does not hide what is under it. Anything else drawn on top at that point (another client's panel, dock, popup or overlay, even one that lets clicks through; a menu; the lock screen) answers none with reason nothing.

request.name: focused
request.description: The active window: the toplevel that last had keyboard focus (it stays active while a panel or popup holds the keyboard), or none with reason nothing. Answered only just after the person's locate key (see the interface description).

request.name: capture

description.summary: a picture of the window just located

request.description: A picture of the window's own content, rendered from that window alone: never its decorations and never anything overlapping it. It fits max_width x max_height, each first held to 16..2048, and is never larger than the window. See the interface description for which window may be captured, and when.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the window, as the most recent answer named it

event.name: window

description.summary: the window there, or the focused window

event.description: app_id and title are each cut to at most 511 bytes, at a character boundary. x, y, width and height are the window's content in layout coordinates, without decorations. A private window's title is empty.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: app id (Wayland) or class (X11); empty if none

event.name: picture
event.description: Premultiplied ARGB8888 (DRM_FORMAT_ARGB8888, little-endian), height rows of stride bytes, in a sealed memory file the client maps read only and closes.

event.name: armed

description.summary: the person pressed the locate key

event.description: The person ran the compositor's locate action (YantrikLocate, bound to a key such as Super+Y). A focused request is answered with the active window within the next two seconds, once. Not sent while the session is locked.
